originality.rationale: Comparison of implication strengths: prior rank-one results classify metricity and give nonmetric examples for transformed exponent t>2, but do not determine the optimal multiplicative quasi-triangle coefficient for t>=3 or prove its equality geometry and exact angular convexity boundary. Sra covers the complementary p>=1 metric regime; Vuong 2026 studies nonsharp spectral/local bounds. Searches using both p and t=2/p parametrizations, the angular cosine-power form, the exact constant, and pure-state aliases found no equivalent/stronger quantitative result. Unsurveyed equivalent formulations remain possible.

value.rationale: The exact dimension-free multiplicative quasi-triangle optimum on the pure-state boundary provides quantitative sharp geometry that existing yes/no metricity results lack. The exponent p=2/3 is the exact angular convexity transition rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; the result identifies the complete extremal configuration and the exact p->0 blow-up. This is nontrivial even though the qualitative triangle failure was known.
